topics.topic: AuditEntry lifecycle semantics when restoring an older backup
questions: What happens to AuditEntries written after the restored backup, since the stated lifecycle permits an entry to disappear only through the owner's dated erasure but an older store backup would not contain them?
Can restoring an older backup remove AuditEntries written after that backup, or must those entries survive the restore as well as the sequence high-water mark?
When an older backup contains audit entries that were subsequently erased, does restoring it make those entries readable again, or must the instance marks preserve their erased lifecycle state?

quotes:
Every change after the backup's instant is
   lost, the audit entries with it; the instance marks are not replaced, so
   numbering continues above every number ever written (A15) and a migration
   closure is never lost: at start Registry writes the closure into the store
   when the marks hold it and the store does not, and the import stays closed
   (R0-79).

The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
   the latest date the owner erased by, before configuring the tokens and
   starting it again.
judgement.why: State 2 says post-backup entries are lost, their sequence numbers remain consumed, and restored entries previously erased are removed again during the owner-only recovery step.

topics.topic: MigrationClosure facts retained by instance marks after restore
questions: Does the outside-store mark hold every MigrationClosure fact—the success instant, owner principal, confirmation id and file digest—or only the fact that import has closed, and if only the latter, what MigrationClosure facts exist after restoring a pre-import backup?
After restoring a backup that predates the import, where do the closure's instant, acting principal, confirmation id and accepted-file digest come from?
Do the instance marks retain every MigrationClosure fact—success instant, acting principal, confirmation id and file digest—or only the fact that import is closed?

quotes:
An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers,
   the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry
   (M09) in one transaction, after recording the closure in the instance
   marks (A15).

Every change after the backup's instant is
   lost, the audit entries with it; the instance marks are not replaced, so
   numbering continues above every number ever written (A15) and a migration
   closure is never lost: at start Registry writes the closure into the store
   when the marks hold it and the store does not, and the import stays closed
   (R0-79).
judgement.why: State 2 records the M10 migration closure itself in the instance marks and reconstructs that closure in the store after a restore, so the marks preserve the closure's complete modeled facts.

topics.topic: Whether imported models survive or are recovered when permanent closure survives restore
questions: If a backup from before the successful import is restored, what happens to the Projects, Customers, Rooms and ArtifactPointers created by that import while the surviving MigrationClosure still causes every further import to be refused?
If a restored backup predates the import, must the imported models also survive or be recovered, or may Registry retain the closure and refuse another import while those models are absent?

If the restored backup predates the successful import, must the imported Projects, Customers, Rooms and ArtifactPointers also remain present, or may the MigrationClosure survive while those imported models disappear and another import remains refused?

quotes:
Right after it Registry makes a backup
   run outside the daily schedule (A18), so a backup holding the import
   exists.

Every change after the backup's instant is
   lost, the audit entries with it; the instance marks are not replaced, so
   numbering continues above every number ever written (A15) and a migration
   closure is never lost: at start Registry writes the closure into the store
   when the marks hold it and the store does not, and the import stays closed
   (R0-79).
judgement.why: State 2 makes an immediate post-import backup available but expressly permits an older restore to lose all later imported records while preserving the closure and keeping import closed.

topics.topic: Persistence boundary and storage location of instance marks
questions: How can the closure be durable outside the store when State 0 defines one instance as holding one store and State 1 enumerates MigrationClosure as Registry's durable model; are instance marks part of that store, a second Registry store, or infrastructure outside Registry?
Are the instance marks part of Registry's one durable store, or does Registry now own a second durable persistence location outside that store?
Are the instance marks part of Registry's one durable store, or does MigrationClosure now exist in a second durable persistence location?

quotes:
Registry records each number in the instance
   marks — a small file in the backup location, apart from the store and the
   backups, which a restore does not replace (A18) — before the entry
   commits;

The instance marks
   there (A15) are made at the first start; marks that cannot be read fail
   the start.
judgement.why: State 2 locates the marks explicitly in a small file in the configured backup location, apart from Registry's store and backups; State 0's one-store decision does not state that no auxiliary persistence file may exist.

topics.topic: Ownership and Registry operations for the audit sequence instance mark
questions: What is the instance mark that owns the last audit sequence number, and which Registry actions create, advance or read it, given that State 1 says its listed models and facts are exhaustive?
